    • Room: NMAP

    What is nmap? Its a networking mapping tool used by a lot of security experts as a starting point for port scanning, in simples terms, most security experts and also the bad people on the tinterweb use it to find open ports, service information, whats running on your network devices etc.

    In this little write up, we will go through the nmap room on tryhackme and explain in more detail and better structured help guide to assist you with learning the nmap room from start to finish with small descriptions for each action/switch.

    Task 1 - Deploy
    - This task is pretty simple (but not required until task 3), so long as your connected to the tryhackme network via vpn, you can deploy a virtual machine on their network, so go ahead hit "Deploy"
    Task 2 - Nmap Quiz (all the answers can be found in nmap -h, but I thought I would do a little explanation for them to)
    Q1: It is asking how you access the help menu for nmap, very simple and in the title for task 2, this will list most common switches used by security professionals
    Q2: Often referred to as a "stealth scan", what is the first switch listed for "Syn Scan" (Answer: -sS). Syn scan is a popular scanning technique used by security experts due to its ability to scan thousands of ports per second on a network and without the need to fully complete its TCP connection, thus the name stealth scan.
    Q3: Not quite as useful but how about a "UDP Scan"? (Answer: -sU). UDP scans are used to perform scans to find out which UDP ports are open and vulnerable to attack.
    Q4: What about operating system detection? (Answer: -O uppercase). It utilises both TCP & UDP to send packets to a specific port, using the information it has gathered, it then compares that information with a database of over 2000 operating systems and return information on the OS and Version of the host.
    Q5: How about service version detection? (Answer: -sV). This technique is used to find what services and versions are running on specific ports to help security professionals find potential vulnerabilities on their network.
    Q6: Most people like to see some output to know that their scan is actually doing things, what is the verbosity flag? (Answer: -v lowercase). When in verbosity mode, you are able to gather more information such as when scans where started, how many hosts are being scanned etc. If run on nmaps birthday, it waill also wish its self happy birthday (Fun fact of thier site!).
    Q7: What about 'very verbose'? (Answer: -vv lowercase). Like above, but if I am correct in thinking, very verbose is much more effective and the preferred method of use by security professionals
    Q8: Sometimes saving output in a common document format can be really handy for reporting, how do we save output in xml format? (Answer: -oX). This allows you to send the output data to an XML file so you can open it from a web based browser such as firefox or google chrome.
    Q9: Aggressive scans can be nice when other scans just aren't getting the output that you want and you really don't care how 'loud' you are, what is the switch for enabling this? (Answer: -A). So what is Aggresive mode? it's a combination of different scans such as OS detection, version detection, script scanning and traceroute, cool huh? While it does have the ability to be easily detected, it can also provide a cyber security expert with a lot of valuable information.
    Q10: How do I set the timing to the max level, sometimes called 'Insane'? (Answer: -T5). There are different levels for timing which are 0-5, 0 being the slowest and 5 being the fastest. By default nmap utilises level T3 when running scans without a timing level set.
    Q11: What about if I want to scan a specific port? (Answer: -p). So as an example, if you wanted to scan a specific port to find if it is open on your network or not, you would do nmap -p22 and this will scan port 22, this will give you a clear picture to whether its filtered through a firewall, open etc
    Q12: How about if I want to scan every port? (Answer: -p-) As the question asks, this basically will scan every port to find which port is open on your network, another good thing is, say you want to scan from 0-2000, you can do nmap -p-2000 and this will scan for any port open up to 2000!
    Q13: What if I want to enable using a script from the nmap scripting engine? For this, just include the first part of the switch without the specification of what script to run. (Answer: --script | -sC ). NMaps scripting engine is definitely one of its better and most richest features allowing security experts to either write their own custom scripts for their needs, or utilise a list of defined categories implemented in to nmap itself.
    Q14: What if I want to run all scripts out of the vulnerability category? (Answer: --script vuln) As I mentioned in Q13 about a defined list of categories implemented into nmap, well vuln (vulnerability) is one of them, what this particular script will do is check for any currently known vulnerabilities and only should produce any data back if one or more was found.
    Q15: What switch should I include if I don't want to ping the host? (Answer: -Pn). According to nmaps help guide, this will treat all host as online and basically skip host discovery and will continue to scan IPs as if they was UP.
    Task 3 - Nmap scanning
    NOTE: If you paid attention to task 2, this will be a breeze but I will help provide the answers still and which question it was in task 2 and use the IP of the server deployed via TryHackMe as the target IP for scanning so for example the IP I have been assigned is: 10.10.213.108.
    Q1: Let's go ahead and start with the basics and perform a syn scan on the box provided. What will this command be without the host IP address? (Answer: nmap -sS) Task 2 - Question 2.
    Q2: After scanning this, how many ports do we find open under 1000? (Answer: 2) nmap -sS 10.10.213.108 will provide the same information as nmap -p-1000 10.10.213.108, this will show only 2 open ports. Task 2 - Question 12.
    Q3: What communication protocol is given for these ports following the port number? (Answer: TCP) See image below, the communication protocol will always show at the side of any open ports found
    Q4: Perform a service version detection scan, what is the version of the software running on port 22? (Answer: 6.6.1p1) So after you run nmap -sV 10.10.213.108 this will give you the data required to find the version your service is running on. Refer back to Task 2 - Question 5.
    Q5: Perform an aggressive scan, what flag isn't set under the results for port 80? (Answer: nmap -A -p80 10.10.213.108) As it says on port 80 only, we can define -A along with -p80 to scan only that port. Task 2, Question 9 for Aggresive mode and question 11 for -p Specific Port.
    Q3: Perform a script scan of vulnerabilities associated with this box, what denial of service (DOS) attack is this box susceptible to? (Answer: http-slowloris-check) I decided to shorten the question down from THM, now using the image below, use command nmap --script vuln (as mentioned in Task 2 Q13 & 14 in regards to defined list and vulnerability being one) baring in mind this will take a while to complete so grab a brew or something and once its complete, as you will see on your screen an output similar to my own with a list of service/s that are vulnerable and to what attack.

    Well done! If you have followed this guide you should of been able to complete the nmap room as well as gain a better understanding on it. I am not claiming I am an expert by any means, even I am still learning about nmap but I would highly recommend checking out nmaps website and reference guide to get in-depth knowledge about every different action nmap does, as well as some examples! I hope you enjoyed my write up but if you do think things could be written out better, please do let me know and I can look into making some changes :D
